findings.evidence: AEMO's 2026 ISP states Stage 2 is a committed project for November 2027. The chart's single 2027 date covers only Stage 2: Stage 1 was completed in late 2024, and Transgrid's own page instead targets NEM integration by the end of 2026. The trunk length now matches a sourced 160 km Stage 1 section exactly, but that is one section of a nine-hundred-kilometre project, and the capacity, syncon and transformer cells conflict on stated source boundaries; line and feeder counts require explicit definitions.

summary.analysis_conclusion: There is no archived reconciled whole-project cost for Project EnergyConnect. The AER approved two separate owner allowances, $457.4m ($2017-18) for ElectraNet and $1,817.9m ($2017-18) for TransGrid, and described the project as a proposed $2.3 billion ($2017-18) contingent project. TransGrid's February 2026 reopener application, citing Contract Failure, now states a forecast cost of $3,628 million (real 2022-23) to complete TransGrid's own NSW component - a proponent forecast, not an AER-approved amount, and not stated to include ElectraNet's SA works. The chart's $4.1 billion still matches only Transgrid's separate social-value claim, a benefit measure, and the chart's 160 km now has an exact but different match: Transgrid's June 2026 completion release states Stage 1 (SA border to Buronga and into Victoria) is 160 km, distinct from the 165 km Dinawan-Wagga Wagga section and from the 900 km whole-route figure both Transgrid's page and the joint ElectraNet/Transgrid project page state. Cost, capacity, trunk km, syncons and transformers require the stated boundary corrections; line and feeder interpretations depend on explicit chart definitions.
summary.capacity: Stage 1 delivered 150 MW in both directions between NSW and SA. AEMO expects the NSW-SA interconnector to increase to 800 MW in both directions after Stage 2, with a further 100 MW VIC-SA. No archived source states 2.2 GW.
summary.completion_date: Stage 1: late 2024 (AEMO 2026), though Transgrid's June 2026 completion release instead says Stage 1 'became operational last year' (i.e. 2025) - a contradiction, not resolved. Stage 2: November 2027 (AEMO 2026), against Transgrid's stated NEM integration by end of 2026; Transgrid's June 2026 release reports the 700 km NSW section construction complete and Stage 2 being energised ahead of inter-network testing
summary.current_status: Committed and under construction. AEMO's 2026 ISP records Stage 1 (Robertstown via Bundey to Buronga) completed in late 2024 and Stage 2 committed for November 2027; Transgrid's own page states construction and initial energisation are complete with NEM integration due by the end of 2026. Transgrid's June 2026 completion release states construction of the 700 km NSW section is complete and Stage 2 (the 540 km Buronga-Wagga Wagga line) is being energised ahead of AEMO's inter-network testing; it also states Stage 1 (160 km, SA border to Buronga and into Victoria) 'became operational last year', which is not consistent with AEMO's 'late 2024' Stage 1 completion date. Transgrid's February 2026 application to reopen its 2023-2028 revenue determination cites Contract Failure (recognised by Transgrid's Board on 25 October 2023) and a resulting forecast cost increase to $3,628 million (real 2022-23) to complete the NSW component; this reopener had not been decided by the AER as at the 2026-09-03 research cutoff.
summary.delivery_status: Stage 1 complete (late 2024); Stage 2 under construction and committed
summary.dependent_projects: Interfaces with HumeLink and VNI West at Wagga Wagga and Dinawan; these are dependencies, not PEC components. The Victorian connection is a 220 kV spur at Red Cliffs.
summary.funding_pathway: AER contingent project determinations under the 2018-23 regulatory control periods, one per owner (both final 28 May 2021)
summary.identity: One Project EnergyConnect delivered jointly by ElectraNet (South Australia) and TransGrid (New South Wales), with a 220 kV spur to Victoria at Red Cliffs. Stage 1 and Stage 2 are components of one project; the SA and NSW owner boundaries are separate regulatory proceedings, not separate projects.

timeline.detail: PEC listed as anticipated with a July 2026 full-capacity date following inter-regional testing; ISP modelling used a July 2025 service date.
Committed project, Stage 1 scheduled December 2024 and Stage 2 July 2027, with capacity release conditional on inter-network testing, market conditions and good test results.
Robertstown (via Bundey) to Buronga completed in late 2024, providing an initial 150 MW transfer capability between NSW and SA. No primary completion instrument was captured.
Stage 2 underway and committed for November 2027; NSW-SA capability expected to increase to 800 MW in both directions after Stage 2.

Construction and initial energisation complete; asset commissioning progressing ahead of inter-network testing and integration into the NEM by the end of 2026; project described as 900 km across three states.

Transgrid's Board recognised and accepted that Contract Failure had occurred, meaning the successful completion of PEC by Elecnor Australia under the existing EPC contract was not possible. Transgrid subsequently identified and evaluated alternative options before entering an Incentivised Completion Cost (ICC) contract with Elecnor Australia in December 2024.

TransGrid applied under NER clause 6A.7.1(a) to reopen its 2023-2028 revenue determination, citing Contract Failure and stating a forecast total capital expenditure to complete PEC (TransGrid's NSW component) of $3,628 million (real 2022-23), against an inflation-adjusted CPA allowance of $2,121 million; the cover letter rounds this to 'the forecast cost to deliver PEC had increased to $3.6 billion.' The reopener amount sought is $1,142 million. Not yet decided by the AER as at the 2026-09-03 research cutoff.

Transgrid and Elecnor Australia completed construction of the 700 km NSW section (1,500+ towers, 10,000+ km of conductor). Stage 2 (the 540 km Buronga-Wagga Wagga line) is being energised following commissioning checks, ahead of AEMO inter-network testing due later in 2026. The release also states Stage 1 (160 km, SA border to Buronga and into Victoria) 'became operational last year' - which does not match AEMO's 'late 2024' Stage 1 completion date.
timeline.event: Transgrid reports EnergyConnect NSW section construction complete

timeline.detail: The joint project page states an approximate total route length of 900 km, an approximate interconnector transfer capacity of 800 MW, and a 700 km NSW section - though its 'Current status' text describes NSW construction as still under way, not complete as Transgrid's own June 2026 completion release states.

warnings.finding: Whether a whole-project cost view for Project EnergyConnect is publishable at all. The archive offers only: a rounded AER descriptive figure of $2.3 billion ($2017-18) at proposal stage; two non-additive owner determinations; an undated-dollar 2020 ISP range of $1,393m-$2,587m; owner proposals; and now TransGrid's February 2026 reopener forecast of $3,628 million (real 2022-23) to complete its NSW component alone, following Contract Failure and pending an AER decision.
warnings.implication: The chart row publishes one cost number for the whole project. The author must decide whether to publish the AER descriptive $2.3 billion ($2017-18) with its basis stated, to publish TransGrid's $3,628m NSW-only reopener forecast with its basis and pending-decision status stated, to publish the owner boundaries separately, or to publish no whole-project cost.

warnings.finding: The chart's $4.1 billion cost cannot be reproduced from any archived cost figure or combination of them. A newer figure is now archived - TransGrid's February 2026 reopener application states a forecast total capital expenditure to complete PEC (its NSW component) of $3,628 million (real 2022-23), rounded in its cover letter to 'about $3.6 billion' - but this also does not match the chart's $4.1bn cell, is on a different boundary (TransGrid's NSW component only) and basis (real 2022-23, not $2017-18), and is a proponent forecast, not an AER-approved amount.
warnings.implication: A social-value benefit estimate is not capital expenditure.
